STRIP CONFIGURATION

Add strips

Same LED count and patch format? Add them all in one go.

By default, only complete LEDs are placed at the end of a universe. Any unused channels are skipped and the next LED starts at address 1 of the next universe. RGBA uses the selected RGB order followed by alpha.
EXPORT

Your map, ready to go.

Inferred line points are included with measured points. Resolume receives one embedded RGB or RGBA fixture per mapped LED. Unmapped LEDs are omitted; their channel addresses stay reserved. Controller outputs start disabled.

Open the map in Resolume

In Arena, open Output → Advanced Output. Use the preset menu to load the XML file. Review the Input Selection, then select your Art-Net controller for each Lumiverse in DMX Output.

The preset follows Arena 7’s XML structure. Verify the setup in your installed Arena version before a show.
QUICK START

From light to layout.

  1. Launch the StripR app

    Download your operating system’s executable from the latest GitHub Release and launch it. The embedded web interface and LED bridge open in your browser; no Node.js installation or separate website is required.

  2. Connect your controller

    In LED controller, select Art-Net or sACN/E1.31 and enter the controller address. For WLED, enable E1.31 unicast with starting universe 1 and Multiple RGB, then select sACN here. StripR remembers the output choice.

    From a phone, use the same Wi-Fi and enter the StripR computer’s LAN address as the local bridge address. Enter a token only if StripR was started with STRIPR_TOKEN.

  3. Define, scan, review

    Add and patch your strips, secure the camera, then start scanning. Shift-click ranges, Ctrl/Cmd-click individual LEDs, or drag a marquee to transform groups. Undo and redo use the standard keyboard shortcuts.

  4. Export your map

    JSON saves the editable project with normalized coordinates. Resolume XML builds DMX Lumiverses with embedded RGB pixel fixtures.

Implement your own bridge

Use the stripr/1 protocol: GET /api/health, POST /api/output, POST /api/configure, POST /api/pixel, and POST /api/blackout. Each pixel command blacks out all other LEDs. See API documentation for payloads, CORS, and acknowledgments.
